name: Battlezone
title: Three boards, three power stories

mains.input: 36 VAC into the Regulator/Audio II PCB (035435-02) on J9 pins 4 and 5, plus +10.3 VDC unregulated on J6
mains.note: International Power Supply 035887-01 has a voltage selection block for 100/120/220/250 V; sheet 1 Side A carries its schematic

rails.+5V logic: LM305 (Q1) with 2N3055 pass transistor (Q3) and TIP32 bias (Q2) on the Regulator/Audio II PCB; adjusted at R8 and sensed remotely at the game PCB
rails.+/-22V: unregulated, straight off the 36VAC bridge CR5-CR8; the audio output stage on the Auxiliary PCB runs on the +22V
rails.+15V / -15V / +5V DAC: generated on the game PCB itself -- VR3 (7815) and VR2 (7805) off +22VDC, VR1 (7915) off -22VDC, for the analog vector generator

indicators.CR2 on the Auxiliary PCB: MV5053 LED through R37 (150R), +5V present -- same designator, different board

adjustment.R8 (+5V): Meter across the game PCB's +5V and GND test points and adjust R8 on the Regulator/Audio II PCB for +5 VDC there, not at the regulator. Then check +5V REG to GND on the Regulator/Audio PCB reads no more than +5.5 VDC; if it reads higher, the gap is harness drop -- clean both sets of edge connectors, then measure GND-to-GND and +5REG-to-+5V between the boards to find which wire is dropping it.

note: The regulator senses at the game PCB through high-impedance +SENSE and -SENSE lines, so it cancels the IR drop along the harness. The consequence for diagnosis is that a tired harness makes the regulator's own output rise while the game PCB still measures 5 V -- the fault shows at the regulator, not where it is.
